iterations.explanation: The design space is organized along the machine learning workflow, beginning with Data Acquisition Strategy, Data Storage Architecture, Data Quality Validation, Data Processing Architecture, and Data Partitioning Strategy; continuing through Feature Representation Strategy, Model Family Selection, Training Procedure, Optimization and Tuning Strategy, Experiment Evaluation Strategy, and Experiment Reproducibility Strategy; and ending with Model Packaging Format, Model Serving Strategy, Deployment Topology, Production Monitoring Strategy, Retraining Strategy, and Release Governance. The dimensions are decision axes rather than lifecycle phases: each asks one architectural question, while its values represent commonly adopted alternatives, rejected practices, or important operational outcomes. Relations emphasize dependencies such as partitioning before training evaluation, serving requirements shaping packaging, and monitoring informing retraining. The taxonomy includes both technical choices and operational controls because production machine learning systems must manage data quality, reproducibility, latency, drift, fairness, cost, reliability, and accountability in addition to predictive accuracy. Rejected values capture recurring practitioner anti-patterns, while outcome values such as silent model degradation capture effects that practitioners must design against rather than select as intentional architectures.

clusters.name: Data Acquisition Strategy
clusters.description: How raw data is obtained and incorporated into the machine learning system. Values answer whether data is collected in batches, streams, or through externally managed sources.

relations.reading: Data Acquisition Strategy constrains Data Storage Architecture
relations.rationale: The arrival pattern, volume, and durability requirements of acquired data limit suitable storage architectures.

relations.reading: Data Acquisition Strategy affects Data Quality Validation
relations.rationale: Streaming, externally sourced, and user-generated data present different completeness, freshness, and trust risks.

values.label: Batch data ingestion
values.description: Periodic loading of accumulated data from files, databases, or exports.

values.label: Streaming data ingestion
values.description: Continuous ingestion of events or records as they are produced.

values.label: External data integration
values.description: Use of third-party, public, partner, or vendor-provided datasets and services.

values.label: Synchronous online acquisition
values.description: Acquisition of features or observations during an online prediction request.

values.label: Uncontrolled data collection
values.description: Ad hoc collection without stable ownership, contracts, lineage, or ingestion controls.

clusters.name: Data Storage Architecture
clusters.description: How raw, curated, feature, and training data are persisted and made accessible. Values answer which storage organization supports the workflow.

relations.reading: Data Storage Architecture affects Data Processing Architecture
relations.rationale: Storage format, locality, and access patterns influence batch and streaming processing choices.

relations.reading: Data Storage Architecture affects Feature Representation Strategy
relations.rationale: The persistence and retrieval model determines whether features can be reused consistently for training and serving.

relations.reading: Data Storage Architecture constrains Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Online serving depends on whether required data and features can be retrieved within latency and availability targets.

values.label: Data lake storage
values.description: Centralized storage of raw and semi-structured data in scalable object or distributed storage.

values.label: Data warehouse storage
values.description: Curated, schema-managed storage optimized for analytical queries and governed datasets.

values.label: Operational database storage
values.description: Persistence in transactional or application databases close to the systems producing or consuming the data.

values.label: Feature store storage
values.description: Specialized offline and online persistence for reusable machine learning features.

values.label: Unmanaged local-file storage
values.description: Scattered files or notebooks used as the system of record for datasets.

clusters.name: Data Quality Validation
clusters.description: How the system detects invalid, incomplete, inconsistent, stale, or anomalous data before it affects training or inference.

relations.reading: Data Quality Validation constrains Data Processing Architecture
relations.rationale: Validation placement and strictness determine where processing gates, quarantines, and remediation paths must exist.

relations.reading: Data Quality Validation affects Training Procedure
relations.rationale: Undetected data defects can alter training distributions, labels, and measured model quality.

relations.reading: Data Quality Validation affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: The checks used before training provide baselines and corresponding checks for production drift and failures.

values.label: Schema and contract validation
values.description: Checks for expected types, fields, ranges, units, and producer contracts.

values.label: Statistical data validation
values.description: Checks distributions, missingness, cardinality, outliers, and changes relative to historical data.

values.label: Semantic and label validation
values.description: Checks domain meaning, annotation consistency, label correctness, and leakage risks.

values.label: Quarantine and remediation
values.description: Isolation of invalid records with correction, replay, or human review workflows.

values.label: Unvalidated ingestion
values.description: Allowing data to flow into training or serving without automated quality gates.

clusters.name: Data Processing Architecture
clusters.description: How raw data is cleaned, joined, transformed, and materialized for downstream use. Values answer whether processing is performed in batch, streaming, or a hybrid architecture.

relations.reading: Data Processing Architecture requires Data Partitioning Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Processing pipelines need a defined separation of training, validation, and test data to avoid contamination.

relations.reading: Data Processing Architecture affects Feature Representation Strategy
relations.rationale: Processing determines transformations, aggregation windows, and the representation available to models.

relations.reading: Data Processing Architecture affects Model Family Selection
relations.rationale: The available scale, latency, and transformed inputs influence feasible model families.

values.label: Batch data processing
values.description: Scheduled transformation and materialization of data in discrete jobs.

values.label: Streaming data processing
values.description: Continuous transformation and aggregation of records as they arrive.

values.label: Hybrid batch-stream processing
values.description: A unified or coordinated design supporting historical batch computation and incremental online updates.

values.label: Notebook-centered processing
values.description: Manual, interactive transformations that are not reproducible or operationally managed.

clusters.name: Data Partitioning Strategy
clusters.description: How data is divided for training, validation, testing, and operational evaluation. Values answer which partitioning scheme prevents leakage while reflecting deployment conditions.

relations.reading: Data Partitioning Strategy constrains Training Procedure
relations.rationale: Training and hyperparameter selection must use partitions without leaking evaluation information.

relations.reading: Data Partitioning Strategy affects Experiment Evaluation Strategy
relations.rationale: The partition scheme determines whether reported metrics estimate generalization to future, unseen, or grouped cases.

values.label: Random holdout partitioning
values.description: Randomly separated training, validation, and test examples under an exchangeability assumption.

values.label: Temporal partitioning
values.description: Training on earlier data and evaluating on later data to simulate future deployment.

values.label: Group-aware partitioning
values.description: Keeping users, devices, entities, or related examples within a single partition.

values.label: Cross-validation partitioning
values.description: Repeated folds used to estimate performance and tune models when data is limited.

values.label: Random leakage-prone partitioning
values.description: Random splitting despite temporal, entity, or duplicate relationships that cause optimistic evaluation.

clusters.name: Feature Representation Strategy
clusters.description: How inputs are represented for learning and inference, including transformation ownership and feature reuse.

relations.reading: Feature Representation Strategy constrains Model Family Selection
relations.rationale: Sparse, dense, sequential, categorical, and multimodal representations support different model families.

relations.reading: Feature Representation Strategy affects Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Preprocessing and feature computation must be packaged consistently with the model or serving environment.

relations.reading: Feature Representation Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Online feature availability and transformation cost directly affect serving latency and correctness.

values.label: Manual domain features
values.description: Human-designed variables derived from domain knowledge and business rules.

values.label: Learned representations
values.description: Embeddings or internal representations learned jointly or largely automatically from data.

values.label: Raw-input representation
values.description: Passing minimally transformed text, images, audio, logs, or other raw modalities to the model.

values.label: Shared reusable features
values.description: Features computed once and consumed consistently by multiple training and serving workloads.

values.label: Training-only feature computation
values.description: Computing transformations during training without an equivalent or versioned serving path.

clusters.name: Model Family Selection
clusters.description: Which broad class of predictive model is used for the task, data modality, and operational constraints.

relations.reading: Model Family Selection affects Training Procedure
relations.rationale: Model families require different optimization algorithms, resources, regularization, and training workflows.

relations.reading: Model Family Selection affects Optimization and Tuning Strategy
relations.rationale: The model family determines the hyperparameters, search spaces, and computational cost of tuning.

relations.reading: Model Family Selection constrains Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Model size, hardware requirements, and inference complexity limit deployment and serving options.

values.label: Linear and generalized linear models
values.description: Linear, logistic, Poisson, or related models with relatively simple parameterizations.

values.label: Tree-based ensemble models
values.description: Decision trees, random forests, gradient-boosted trees, and related ensembles.

values.label: Deep neural networks
values.description: Multi-layer neural architectures for structured, unstructured, or multimodal data.

values.label: Probabilistic and Bayesian models
values.description: Models that explicitly represent uncertainty, distributions, or prior knowledge.

values.label: Nearest-neighbor and retrieval models
values.description: Prediction or ranking based on similarity search over stored examples or representations.

values.label: Single universal model family
values.description: Using one model family regardless of task characteristics, data modality, or operational constraints.

clusters.name: Training Procedure
clusters.description: How model parameters are fitted, including computational execution, initialization, regularization, and resource use.

relations.reading: Training Procedure co-occurs with Optimization and Tuning Strategy
relations.rationale: Training execution and hyperparameter optimization are usually designed as one experimentation and compute workflow.

relations.reading: Training Procedure affects Experiment Evaluation Strategy
relations.rationale: Training randomness, checkpointing, early stopping, and repeatability affect the reliability of evaluation.

relations.reading: Training Procedure affects Experiment Reproducibility Strategy
relations.rationale: The procedure determines which code, data, seeds, environments, and artifacts must be captured for reproduction.

values.label: Single-machine training
values.description: Training within the memory and compute capacity of one machine.

values.label: Distributed data-parallel training
values.description: Replicated model workers process data partitions and synchronize parameter updates.

values.label: Distributed model-parallel training
values.description: Model parameters or layers are partitioned across devices or machines.

values.label: Transfer learning and fine-tuning
values.description: Starting from a pretrained model and adapting it to a target task or domain.

values.label: Manual one-off training
values.description: Training performed without repeatable jobs, versioned inputs, or automated artifact capture.

clusters.name: Optimization and Tuning Strategy
clusters.description: How model objectives, hyperparameters, architectures, and operating thresholds are selected.

relations.reading: Optimization and Tuning Strategy requires Experiment Evaluation Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Tuning needs a reliable metric, validation protocol, and objective before alternatives can be compared.

relations.reading: Optimization and Tuning Strategy affects Experiment Reproducibility Strategy
relations.rationale: Search spaces, trials, seeds, and selected configurations must be recorded to reproduce the chosen model.

relations.reading: Optimization and Tuning Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Optimization may trade accuracy for latency, memory, throughput, or calibration requirements in production.

values.label: Manual hyperparameter tuning
values.description: Practitioner-directed adjustment based on domain knowledge and observed experiments.

values.label: Grid or random search
values.description: Systematic evaluation of configurations from a defined hyperparameter space.

values.label: Bayesian optimization
values.description: Adaptive selection of trials using a surrogate model of validation performance.

values.label: Multi-objective optimization
values.description: Selection against multiple objectives such as quality, latency, cost, fairness, or robustness.

values.label: Accuracy-only optimization
values.description: Selecting models solely by an offline accuracy metric while ignoring operational or social constraints.

clusters.name: Experiment Evaluation Strategy
clusters.description: How candidate models are compared and judged before release, including metrics, baselines, uncertainty, and testing conditions.

relations.reading: Experiment Evaluation Strategy affects Experiment Reproducibility Strategy
relations.rationale: Evaluation artifacts, datasets, metrics, and randomization must be recorded to reproduce conclusions.

relations.reading: Experiment Evaluation Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Deployment decisions depend on whether offline evaluation reflects online latency, traffic, and business outcomes.

relations.reading: Experiment Evaluation Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Offline metrics and acceptance thresholds establish production monitoring targets and alert baselines.

values.label: Offline metric evaluation
values.description: Comparison using held-out data and task-specific predictive metrics.

values.label: Slice-based evaluation
values.description: Evaluation across demographic, geographic, temporal, behavioral, or other important subgroups.

values.label: Simulation and replay evaluation
values.description: Testing against reconstructed historical sequences, environments, or user interactions.

values.label: Online controlled experimentation
values.description: Comparison through shadow, canary, A/B, or other controlled production exposure.

values.label: Offline-only acceptance
values.description: Releasing a model based solely on offline metrics without operational or representative online testing.

clusters.name: Experiment Reproducibility Strategy
clusters.description: How code, data, environments, configurations, randomness, and artifacts are versioned and recoverable across experiments.

relations.reading: Experiment Reproducibility Strategy affects Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: A reproducible model requires packaging the exact model artifact, dependencies, preprocessing, and configuration.

relations.reading: Experiment Reproducibility Strategy affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Automated retraining requires repeatable pipelines and traceable data and model lineage.

values.label: Versioned experiment tracking
values.description: Tracking runs, parameters, metrics, datasets, code versions, and produced artifacts.

values.label: Containerized environment capture
values.description: Capturing runtime dependencies and execution environments in reproducible images or environments.

values.label: Data and model lineage
values.description: Tracing deployed models to source data, transformations, training runs, approvals, and dependencies.

values.label: Reproducible randomization
values.description: Controlling or recording seeds and nondeterministic execution where repeatability matters.

values.label: Untracked experimentation
values.description: Relying on notebooks, local files, or memory to identify how a model was produced.

clusters.name: Model Packaging Format
clusters.description: How a trained model and its required preprocessing, dependencies, metadata, and signatures are represented for deployment.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Format requires Model Serving Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Packaging must target the serving runtime, supported operators, serialization constraints, and interface requirements.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Format affects Deployment Topology
relations.rationale: Artifact size, runtime dependencies, and hardware requirements influence where and how the model can be deployed.

values.label: Framework-native model artifact
values.description: Serialization in the training framework's native format with its associated runtime.

values.label: Portable interchange model
values.description: Export to a framework-neutral representation supported by multiple runtimes.

values.label: Containerized inference artifact
values.description: Model, preprocessing, runtime, and dependencies bundled into a deployable container image.

values.label: Model-plus-feature bundle
values.description: Packaging the model together with feature transformations, schemas, and serving signatures.

values.label: Training-environment deployment
values.description: Deploying a model by copying an incomplete training environment without a stable inference contract.

clusters.name: Model Serving Strategy
clusters.description: How predictions are exposed and computed for consumers. Values answer whether inference is performed synchronously, asynchronously, in batches, or at the edge.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy constrains Deployment Topology
relations.rationale: Latency, throughput, availability, and connectivity requirements determine viable deployment locations and communication patterns.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Serving mode determines observable request, latency, failure, feature, and prediction signals.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Prediction feedback availability and serving traffic determine how retraining data and triggers are collected.

values.label: Online synchronous inference
values.description: Returning a prediction during a request-response interaction with a latency objective.

values.label: Asynchronous inference
values.description: Submitting prediction work to a queue or job and receiving results later.

values.label: Batch inference
values.description: Generating predictions for accumulated records on a schedule or demand.

values.label: Edge inference
values.description: Running inference near the data source or user device to reduce latency, bandwidth, or connectivity dependence.

values.label: Embedded inference
values.description: Including a model directly inside an application, device, or compiled software component.

values.label: Unbounded synchronous inference
values.description: Making every prediction request wait for an unconstrained model computation or dependency chain.

clusters.name: Deployment Topology
clusters.description: Where model computation and supporting components run and how they are scaled and isolated in production.

relations.reading: Deployment Topology affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Distributed, edge, and managed deployments expose different telemetry, ownership, and observability boundaries.

relations.reading: Deployment Topology affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Deployment boundaries affect access to feedback, data, compute, and the mechanism for replacing model versions.

values.label: Centralized cloud deployment
values.description: Serving and operating models in centrally managed cloud infrastructure.

values.label: Managed machine learning platform
values.description: Using a provider-managed training, registry, endpoint, or pipeline service.

values.label: On-premises deployment
values.description: Running model infrastructure within organization-controlled data centers or private infrastructure.

values.label: Edge and federated deployment
values.description: Distributing inference or training across devices, sites, or data owners with limited centralization.

values.label: Single-host production deployment
values.description: Running a production model without redundancy, isolation, or managed scaling.

clusters.name: Production Monitoring Strategy
clusters.description: How deployed machine learning systems are observed for service health, data and concept drift, model quality, fairness, security, and business impact.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Drift, degradation, failures, and feedback signals can trigger investigation, rollback, or retraining.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Release Governance
relations.rationale: Monitoring evidence informs approval, rollback, incident response, and continued operation of model versions.

values.label: Service health monitoring
values.description: Monitoring availability, latency, throughput, errors, resource use, and dependency health.

values.label: Data and feature drift monitoring
values.description: Detecting changes in input distributions, missingness, freshness, schemas, and feature relationships.

values.label: Prediction and concept drift monitoring
values.description: Monitoring prediction distributions and changes in the relationship between inputs, predictions, and outcomes.

values.label: Outcome and fairness monitoring
values.description: Measuring delayed outcomes, business metrics, subgroup performance, and fairness indicators.

values.label: Unobservable deployment
values.description: Operating a model without telemetry, feedback collection, or checks for production degradation.

values.label: Silent model degradation
values.description: Outcome of distribution shift, stale data, feedback loops, or changing user behavior that reduces model usefulness.

clusters.name: Retraining Strategy
clusters.description: How and when models are updated after initial deployment. Values answer what triggers retraining and how model replacement is coordinated.

relations.reading: Retraining Strategy requires Release Governance to be decided first
relations.rationale: Automated or manual retraining still requires approval, validation, rollback, and accountability rules before replacement.

relations.reading: Retraining Strategy requires Experiment Reproducibility Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Repeated training needs versioned data, code, environments, and lineage to produce trustworthy updates.

relations.reading: Retraining Strategy is affected by Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Monitoring signals determine whether retraining is scheduled, drift-triggered, performance-triggered, or unnecessary.

values.label: Scheduled retraining
values.description: Retraining at fixed calendar or data-volume intervals.

values.label: Drift-triggered retraining
values.description: Retraining initiated when monitored input, feature, prediction, or outcome distributions change materially.

values.label: Performance-triggered retraining
values.description: Retraining initiated when measured model quality or business performance falls below a threshold.

values.label: Continuous or online learning
values.description: Updating model parameters incrementally as new labeled or weakly labeled data arrives.

values.label: Manual retraining
values.description: Retraining initiated and orchestrated by practitioners after review of evidence or a business request.

values.label: Unreviewed automatic replacement
values.description: Replacing a production model automatically without validation, approval, or rollback controls.

clusters.name: Release Governance
clusters.description: How model versions are approved, exposed, rolled back, and held accountable during production operation.

relations.reading: Release Governance constrains Deployment Topology
relations.rationale: Approval, isolation, access control, and rollback requirements constrain deployment mechanisms and environments.

relations.reading: Release Governance affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Canary, shadow, champion-challenger, and rollback practices shape how serving exposes model versions.

relations.reading: Release Governance constrains Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Governance controls limit when retrained models can replace approved production versions.

values.label: Manual approval gates
values.description: Human review and authorization before a model proceeds between environments or into production.

values.label: Automated policy gates
values.description: Automated checks for quality, security, fairness, reproducibility, and operational requirements.

values.label: Canary and shadow release
values.description: Limited or non-user-facing exposure used to validate a new model before broad rollout.

values.label: Champion-challenger release
values.description: Comparing a candidate model against the currently approved model under controlled production conditions.

values.label: Rollback-capable versioning
values.description: Retaining deployable prior versions and the ability to restore them quickly.

values.label: Uncontrolled model release
values.description: Deploying model artifacts directly without approval, staged exposure, version tracking, or rollback.

values.description: Adaptive selection of trials using a surrogate model of validation performance.

values.label: Multi-objective optimization
values.description: Selection against multiple objectives such as quality, latency, cost, fairness, or robustness.

values.label: Accuracy-only optimization
values.description: Selecting models solely by an offline accuracy metric while ignoring operational or social constraints.

selected_clusters.name: Experiment Evaluation Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How candidate models are compared and judged before release, including metrics, baselines, uncertainty, and testing conditions.

relations.reading: Experiment Evaluation Strategy affects Experiment Reproducibility Strategy
relations.rationale: Evaluation artifacts, datasets, metrics, and randomization must be recorded to reproduce conclusions.

relations.reading: Experiment Evaluation Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Deployment decisions depend on whether offline evaluation reflects online latency, traffic, and business outcomes.

relations.reading: Experiment Evaluation Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Offline metrics and acceptance thresholds establish production monitoring targets and alert baselines.

values.label: Offline metric evaluation
values.description: Comparison using held-out data and task-specific predictive metrics.

values.label: Slice-based evaluation
values.description: Evaluation across demographic, geographic, temporal, behavioral, or other important subgroups.

values.label: Simulation and replay evaluation
values.description: Testing against reconstructed historical sequences, environments, or user interactions.

values.label: Online controlled experimentation
values.description: Comparison through shadow, canary, A/B, or other controlled production exposure.

values.label: Offline-only acceptance
values.description: Releasing a model based solely on offline metrics without operational or representative online testing.

selected_clusters.name: Experiment Reproducibility Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How code, data, environments, configurations, randomness, and artifacts are versioned and recoverable across experiments.

relations.reading: Experiment Reproducibility Strategy affects Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: A reproducible model requires packaging the exact model artifact, dependencies, preprocessing, and configuration.

relations.reading: Experiment Reproducibility Strategy affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Automated retraining requires repeatable pipelines and traceable data and model lineage.

values.label: Versioned experiment tracking
values.description: Tracking runs, parameters, metrics, datasets, code versions, and produced artifacts.

values.label: Containerized environment capture
values.description: Capturing runtime dependencies and execution environments in reproducible images or environments.

values.label: Data and model lineage
values.description: Tracing deployed models to source data, transformations, training runs, approvals, and dependencies.

values.label: Reproducible randomization
values.description: Controlling or recording seeds and nondeterministic execution where repeatability matters.

values.label: Untracked experimentation
values.description: Relying on notebooks, local files, or memory to identify how a model was produced.

selected_clusters.name: Model Packaging Format
selected_clusters.description: How a trained model and its required preprocessing, dependencies, metadata, and signatures are represented for deployment.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Format requires Model Serving Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Packaging must target the serving runtime, supported operators, serialization constraints, and interface requirements.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Format affects Deployment Topology
relations.rationale: Artifact size, runtime dependencies, and hardware requirements influence where and how the model can be deployed.

values.label: Framework-native model artifact
values.description: Serialization in the training framework's native format with its associated runtime.

values.label: Portable interchange model
values.description: Export to a framework-neutral representation supported by multiple runtimes.

values.label: Containerized inference artifact
values.description: Model, preprocessing, runtime, and dependencies bundled into a deployable container image.

values.label: Model-plus-feature bundle
values.description: Packaging the model together with feature transformations, schemas, and serving signatures.

values.label: Training-environment deployment
values.description: Deploying a model by copying an incomplete training environment without a stable inference contract.

selected_clusters.name: Model Serving Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How predictions are exposed and computed for consumers. Values answer whether inference is performed synchronously, asynchronously, in batches, or at the edge.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy constrains Deployment Topology
relations.rationale: Latency, throughput, availability, and connectivity requirements determine viable deployment locations and communication patterns.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Serving mode determines observable request, latency, failure, feature, and prediction signals.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Prediction feedback availability and serving traffic determine how retraining data and triggers are collected.

values.label: Online synchronous inference
values.description: Returning a prediction during a request-response interaction with a latency objective.

values.label: Asynchronous inference
values.description: Submitting prediction work to a queue or job and receiving results later.

values.label: Batch inference
values.description: Generating predictions for accumulated records on a schedule or demand.

values.label: Edge inference
values.description: Running inference near the data source or user device to reduce latency, bandwidth, or connectivity dependence.

values.label: Embedded inference
values.description: Including a model directly inside an application, device, or compiled software component.

values.label: Unbounded synchronous inference
values.description: Making every prediction request wait for an unconstrained model computation or dependency chain.

selected_clusters.name: Deployment Topology
selected_clusters.description: Where model computation and supporting components run and how they are scaled and isolated in production.

relations.reading: Deployment Topology affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Distributed, edge, and managed deployments expose different telemetry, ownership, and observability boundaries.

relations.reading: Deployment Topology affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Deployment boundaries affect access to feedback, data, compute, and the mechanism for replacing model versions.

values.label: Centralized cloud deployment
values.description: Serving and operating models in centrally managed cloud infrastructure.

values.label: Managed machine learning platform
values.description: Using a provider-managed training, registry, endpoint, or pipeline service.

values.label: On-premises deployment
values.description: Running model infrastructure within organization-controlled data centers or private infrastructure.

values.label: Edge and federated deployment
values.description: Distributing inference or training across devices, sites, or data owners with limited centralization.

values.label: Single-host production deployment
values.description: Running a production model without redundancy, isolation, or managed scaling.

selected_clusters.name: Production Monitoring Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How deployed machine learning systems are observed for service health, data and concept drift, model quality, fairness, security, and business impact.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Drift, degradation, failures, and feedback signals can trigger investigation, rollback, or retraining.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Release Governance
relations.rationale: Monitoring evidence informs approval, rollback, incident response, and continued operation of model versions.

values.label: Service health monitoring
values.description: Monitoring availability, latency, throughput, errors, resource use, and dependency health.

values.label: Data and feature drift monitoring
values.description: Detecting changes in input distributions, missingness, freshness, schemas, and feature relationships.

values.label: Prediction and concept drift monitoring
values.description: Monitoring prediction distributions and changes in the relationship between inputs, predictions, and outcomes.

values.label: Outcome and fairness monitoring
values.description: Measuring delayed outcomes, business metrics, subgroup performance, and fairness indicators.

values.label: Unobservable deployment
values.description: Operating a model without telemetry, feedback collection, or checks for production degradation.

values.label: Silent model degradation
values.description: Outcome of distribution shift, stale data, feedback loops, or changing user behavior that reduces model usefulness.

selected_clusters.name: Retraining Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How and when models are updated after initial deployment. Values answer what triggers retraining and how model replacement is coordinated.

relations.reading: Retraining Strategy requires Release Governance to be decided first
relations.rationale: Automated or manual retraining still requires approval, validation, rollback, and accountability rules before replacement.

relations.reading: Retraining Strategy requires Experiment Reproducibility Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Repeated training needs versioned data, code, environments, and lineage to produce trustworthy updates.

relations.reading: Retraining Strategy is affected by Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Monitoring signals determine whether retraining is scheduled, drift-triggered, performance-triggered, or unnecessary.

values.label: Scheduled retraining
values.description: Retraining at fixed calendar or data-volume intervals.

values.label: Drift-triggered retraining
values.description: Retraining initiated when monitored input, feature, prediction, or outcome distributions change materially.

values.label: Performance-triggered retraining
values.description: Retraining initiated when measured model quality or business performance falls below a threshold.

values.label: Continuous or online learning
values.description: Updating model parameters incrementally as new labeled or weakly labeled data arrives.

values.label: Manual retraining
values.description: Retraining initiated and orchestrated by practitioners after review of evidence or a business request.

values.label: Unreviewed automatic replacement
values.description: Replacing a production model automatically without validation, approval, or rollback controls.

selected_clusters.name: Release Governance
selected_clusters.description: How model versions are approved, exposed, rolled back, and held accountable during production operation.

relations.reading: Release Governance constrains Deployment Topology
relations.rationale: Approval, isolation, access control, and rollback requirements constrain deployment mechanisms and environments.

relations.reading: Release Governance affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Canary, shadow, champion-challenger, and rollback practices shape how serving exposes model versions.

relations.reading: Release Governance constrains Retraining Strategy
relations.rationale: Governance controls limit when retrained models can replace approved production versions.

values.label: Manual approval gates
values.description: Human review and authorization before a model proceeds between environments or into production.

values.label: Automated policy gates
values.description: Automated checks for quality, security, fairness, reproducibility, and operational requirements.

values.label: Canary and shadow release
values.description: Limited or non-user-facing exposure used to validate a new model before broad rollout.

values.label: Champion-challenger release
values.description: Comparing a candidate model against the currently approved model under controlled production conditions.

values.label: Rollback-capable versioning
values.description: Retaining deployable prior versions and the ability to restore them quickly.

values.label: Uncontrolled model release
values.description: Deploying model artifacts directly without approval, staged exposure, version tracking, or rollback.
